    AI Overview
    No, an amateur has never won the Masters Tournament. While amateurs are invited annually and compete for the Low Amateur title, none have captured the green jacket. The best finishes were runners-up, including Ken Venturi (1956), Charlie Coe (1961), and Frank Stranahan (1947). 
    Key Historical Amateur Highlights: 
    • Closest Finish: Ken Venturi led after 54 holes in 1956 but shot a final-round 80 to finish one shot behind Jack Burke Jr..
    • Billy Joe Patton (1954): Finished 3rd, one stroke out of a Ben Hogan-Sam Snead playoff.
    • Recent Performance: Sam Bennett impressed in 2023, finishing T-16 and holding a spot in the top-10 into the final round
      .
    • Top Finishes: Several amateurs have made significant runs, such as Charlie Coe finishing tied for 2nd in 1961 and 4th in 1957. 
    Amateurs who qualify are playing for prestige and the "Silver Cup" for Low Amateur, as they are not eligible for cash prizes.

    Who was the youngest to win the Masters?

    AI Overview
    Tiger Woods is the youngest winner of the Masters Tournament, securing his first green jacket in 1997 at the age of 21 years, 3 months, and 14 days. He won by a record-breaking margin of 12 strokes. 
    • Youngest Winner: Tiger Woods (21y 3m 14d) in 1997.
    • Previous Record Holder: Seve Ballesteros (23 years old) in 1980.
    • Other Young Winners: Jordan Spieth was 21 when he won in 2015, just slightly older than Woods.
    • Youngest Player to Compete: Guan Tianlang (14 years old) in 2013. 
    Woods also holds the record for the lowest 72-hole score in Masters history, set during that same 1997 victory
    .
